Early Latter-day Saints distinguished between sealings for both time and eternity and sealings that were for eternity only. Eternity-only sealings indicated relationships in the next life alone. These sealings may have provided a way to create an eternal bond or link between Joseph’s family and other families within the Church. See “Plural Marriage in Kirtland and Nauvoo,” Gospel Topics Essay,topics.ChurchofJesusChrist.org.
Zina Huntington Jacobs, autobiographical sketch, Zina Card Brown Family Collection, Church History Library, Salt Lake City; spelling modernized.

Early participants in plural marriage kept few records of the practice. Available historical sources do not give us a clear understanding of the nature and timing of Zina’s marriages. Concerning Zina’s views on the state of her marriage to Henry, see “Evidence from Zina D. Huntington-Young,”Saints’ Herald,vol. 52, no. 2 (Jan. 11, 1905), 29.
See Topics:Winter Quarters;Plural Marriage in Utah. Henry Jacobs was one of many men holding the office of Seventy to be called on missions at this time.
